items.name: Applied Materials
items.why: Ranked first: meets all nine decided tests.

items.name: Fastenal
items.why: Also meets all nine decided tests, with an unbroken dividend record.

items.name: Costco
items.why: Meets eight of nine decided tests; only financial strength (the current ratio) fails.

items.name: Microsoft
items.why: Passes every decided test except financial strength.

items.name: Apple Inc.
items.why: Fails the dividend record (2011 was unpaid) and financial strength; passes the other decided tests.

items.name: Nvidia
items.why: Strong growth and returns, but the dividend record fails (2012 was unpaid) and owner earnings is a data gap.

items.name: Meta Platforms
items.why: Began paying a dividend in 2024, so the dividend record fails; every other decided test passes.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson
items.why: A long dividend record; the margin test is a data gap because the filings tag no operating income.

items.name: Procter & Gamble
items.why: Consumer staples with a long dividend record, a counterpart to Coca-Cola.

items.name: McDonald's
items.why: Negative shareholders' equity: the return-on-equity test is marked not meaningful and the debt test fails.

items.name: Caterpillar Inc.
items.why: A cyclical industrial: the earnings-stability test fails because of one loss year, 2016.

items.name: ExxonMobil
items.why: A new holding company took over the registration in 2026; the figures come from its predecessor, Exxon Mobil Corp, and the page says so.

items.name: Berkshire Hathaway
items.why: Large insurance operations inside an industrial group, so its consolidated figures carry a note, and too few tests are decided to rank it.

items.name: UnitedHealth Group
items.why: Classed by GICS as an ordinary company, not an insurer, so every test applies.

items.name: MetLife
items.why: Insurer rules: four tests do not apply, and the page says why.

items.name: Goldman Sachs
items.why: Treated as a bank (no current assets or operating income) by a rule for the broker-dealer sub-industry.

items.name: Prologis
items.why: A REIT: the rules are unchanged, with a note that its debt is structural; its dividend record depends on reading the right per-share tag.

items.name: Realty Income
items.why: A monthly-dividend REIT: several tests are data gaps, so too few are decided to rank it.

items.name: NextEra Energy
items.why: The debt test uses Graham's utility variant (debt up to twice equity).

items.name: Vistra Corp.
items.why: Not rate-regulated, so the utility variant does not apply; a note says so.

items.name: The Coca-Cola Company
items.why: One of the five companies the rules were built and checked on: an ordinary company with a long, unbroken dividend record.

items.name: JPMorgan Chase
items.why: The bank among them: four tests do not apply, and the page says why.

items.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
items.why: Two share classes analysed once, and a dividend that began only in 2024.

items.name: Tesla, Inc.
items.why: Loss years and no dividend, so several tests fail for plain reasons.

items.name: Duke Energy
items.why: The utility: the debt test uses Graham's variant (debt up to twice equity).
